argument_summary: The current record supports a narrower position than full clean compliance: certification can be defended as a launch-readiness decision because aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and recognized governance guidance permits deployment with documented limitations plus ongoing measurement and monitoring. The disputed point is not whether overall readiness is positive, but whether the named small-business onboarding gap required disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch. On the admissible record, that predicate remains unresolved rather than disproven. The strongest supportable audit treatment is therefore caveated compliance for certification, not escalation based solely on a broader claim that aggregate readiness evidence is irrelevant.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to support this position. The narrower request is governance efficiency: where aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, remaining uncertainty can be handled through explicit caveat and monitoring rather than immediate escalation, unless the auditor is determining that policy requires a binary non-compliance finding on the unresolved disclosure predicate.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not say every residual weakness blocks certification. It says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record shows evidence both ways on materiality weight: product characterizes the affected traffic as 6% of projected first-month volume, while the same segment is also named in two paid pilot commitments and has an open legal disclosure question. That means the clean-compliance predicate is not established, but it also means the record can be framed as unresolved materiality within an otherwise passing release, which supports a caveated certification treatment rather than treating the entire certification rationale as unsupported.
concessions: The current record does not establish clean satisfaction of the disclosure-or-risk-acceptance requirement.
The named small-business onboarding segment missing target by 1.3 percentage points and appearing in two paid pilot commitments is adverse evidence on materiality.
The open legal review weakens any claim that certification is fully policy-compliant without caveat.
General governance-framework support for monitoring does not substitute for case-specific satisfaction of the release policy.
